B is stronger on the plant managers' decision: its table makes the ask to approve three changes explicit. However, B contradicts itself on a slide title (61% vs. 'about 60%'), adds an unsupported 'cheap' claim and an assumed 10-minute slot, and runs longer into a drafted deck, so A is cleaner and more faithful to the supplied facts. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is narrowly better. Its table gives every item one concrete home, and the whole answer is built around the decision the plant managers must make: approving the three changes, with an owner and start date on the final slide. A's main flaw is a slide title that says 61% next to its own calculation of about 60%, and it assumes a 10-minute slot. B is clean and well organized, but it ties content less directly to the managers' decision and assumes hour-by-hour data exists for a time chart.
